name: Digital Crossroad

profile.reading:
Digital Crossroad's Indiana facility, known as DX-1, sits in Hammond, Indiana, on the state line with Illinois and less than thirty minutes from downtown Chicago. The site is an adaptive reuse of the former State Line Generating Plant, a coal fired power station that operated on the Lake Michigan shoreline through much of the twentieth century before its retirement, and the surrounding campus includes a 10,000 square foot technology incubator housed in the former State Line Archway building, a structure the operator notes historically served as office space connected to Thomas Edison. Converting a retired power plant site into a data center campus is a pattern seen at a handful of former utility properties around the country, since the sites already carry heavy duty electrical infrastructure and interconnections that a new data center can reuse rather than build from scratch.

DX-1 itself is a 105,000 square foot building with more than 72,000 square feet of data hall space available to customers. Digital Crossroad states the facility is built to Tier III concurrently maintainable standards, supports up to 20 megawatts of critical IT load, and can draw on a substation with more than 100 megawatts of on site capacity for future phases, with individual racks supporting up to 25 kilowatts of density. The operator reports a design power usage effectiveness of 1.15, a relatively efficient figure that it attributes in part to using Lake Michigan water side economization for cooling alongside outside air cooling and Munters refrigerant based units, reducing reliance on mechanical chilling for much of the year. The facility holds ISO 27001 and SOC 2 certifications, common benchmarks for information security and operational controls in colocation.

On connectivity, Digital Crossroad advertises being fewer than twelve fiber route miles from 350 East Cermak Road in Chicago, one of the Midwest's major carrier hotels, with access to more than 1,700 dark fiber strands and multiple Tier 1 carriers at sub two millisecond latency to that hub. Beyond the data center itself, the company has described plans for a 4,000 square foot smart greenhouse developed in partnership with Purdue University Northwest, suggesting an interest in agricultural technology tied to the campus's land or waste heat, though details of that project's status are not published. Digital Crossroad describes itself as a wholesale colocation company run by industry veterans, but does not publish a founding date or name specific customers on its site.

reading: Digital Crossroad is a privately held wholesale colocation company headquartered in Hammond, Indiana, on the Illinois-Indiana state line less than 30 minutes from downtown Chicago. Its DX-1 facility offers up to 20 megawatts of IT capacity, backed by an onsite electrical substation with more than 100 megawatts of total available capacity, positioning the site for substantial future expansion. The company describes itself as a team of industry veterans focused on sustainable data center solutions that reduce environmental and economic cost. Data center trade press has reported that CoreWeave, the AI cloud infrastructure company, is developing a 180 megawatt data center at a campus referred to as Digital Crossroads in Hammond, Indiana, a naming variation this registry has not fully reconciled against the Digital Crossroad operator name, though the shared Hammond, Indiana location makes it highly likely this refers to the same site undergoing major expansion. This registry treats that CoreWeave connection as a strong lead to verify and record with full detail during the facility-research phase rather than a confirmed fact based on the operator's own disclosure. Digital Crossroad's Chicago-adjacent Indiana location, offering lower-cost land and power near a major metro market, follows a pattern seen elsewhere in the Midwest data center industry.
